name: Romantic nationalism
summary: Romantic nationalism holds that a state's legitimacy comes from the organic unity of a people, defined by shared language, culture, history and customs, rather than from a dynasty or empire. It treasures folklore, national epics and the vernacular as carriers of the national spirit, and demands self-determination and often unification for each nation. In its mainstream nineteenth-century form it was liberal, democratic and republican, placing duty to humanity above narrow patriotism, though a racialised and chauvinist strand also grew from it.
scope: The mainstream nineteenth-century liberal-cultural strand, based on Herder, Mazzini's The Duties of Man, the Grimms' folklore project and the 1848 revolutions, with Mickiewicz's Polish messianism as a religious variant. It excludes the later volkisch and racial nationalism, fascism and twentieth-century ethnic chauvinism, which are noted only where they split adherents. Economic, modern-technology and social-policy statements were mostly never addressed and are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Giuseppe Mazzini
keyFigures.role: Italian republican nationalist and author of The Duties of Man

keyFigures.name: Johann Gottlieb Fichte

sources.title: Romantic nationalism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, language and folklore emphasis, religion, racialised strands, Fichte, Grimm, Mickiewicz, 1848.

sources.title: The Duties of Man, Chapter V: Duties Towards Your Country
sources.author: Giuseppe Mazzini
sources.usedFor: Nations as God-given units, humanity before country, will of the people, equality, rejection of birth privilege, education, work and franchise.

sources.title: Johann Gottfried von Herder
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Herder's cultural pluralism, anti-colonialism, rejection of race and universal reason, and liberal-republican politics.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Mazzini wanted education and work guaranteed to every citizen; healthcare is not addressed, so this is inferred from his social-minimum concern.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Mazzini stressed fair labour and association, but the movement had no wage-law doctrine and its adherents ranged from liberals to conservatives.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Economics was not a defining concern; the movement spanned free-trade liberals and protectionist nationalists such as List's followers.

public-ownership.rationale: Mazzini favoured worker association over state socialism, and other nationalists took no stand; adherents split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No tax doctrine; Mazzini's call for the labouring classes' welfare is too general to infer a position on rates.

unions-good.rationale: Mazzini promoted workers' associations as part of national life, though he opposed class war; inferred as mild support.

property-fundamental.rationale: Mazzini accepted property but subordinated it to social duty; the movement as a whole did not centre on it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations were not an issue for the movement; no basis to infer a position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Mazzini held that a nation is incomplete while citizens lack education and work, which cuts against cutting social provision.

worker-ownership.rationale: Mazzini endorsed producer cooperation, but most romantic nationalists never addressed it; split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Liberal nationalists such as Mazzini were conspirators who suffered police surveillance and prized free association; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: An anachronistic question the movement never addressed; no principle clearly applies.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Mazzini's liberal nationalists prized free expression against censorious dynastic regimes; inferred, though ethnic hostility was common among later strands.

strong-leader.rationale: Mazzini wanted laws expressing the whole nation's will via a people of equals; strong-man shortcuts fit the later militarist strands only.

state-harmful.rationale: Herder favoured weak, loosely federated government but not abolishing it, and Mazzini wanted a republic; the nation needs a state, so the claim is rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist movements armed citizens for liberation, but modern gun control is anachronistic.

empower-police-military.rationale: Herder opposed militarised states while later nationalists built national armies; the movement is split.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; moral views among adherents ranged from Christian to bohemian.

decide-locally.rationale: Herder favoured loose federations of local government, yet most nationalists wanted a unified national state; weak lean to agree.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy was not a concern of the movement; no clear inference.

traditional-family.rationale: Folk tradition and Christian values underpinned national culture for most adherents, though the movement did not centre on family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from its stress on traditional folk customs and Christian-influenced culture; anachronistic, so low confidence.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the movement's religious-traditional cultural tone and its concern for national continuity; never addressed.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion was part of national identity for many strands, e.g. Mickiewicz's Christ of Nations and the Polish church, and Mazzini grounded nations in God.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; Herder rejected race and colonialism, but the 19th-century movement did not address redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its celebration of folk tradition and organic national character; not discussed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultivating national language, folklore, epics and customs as the carrier of a people's spirit is the movement's defining activity.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement drove revolutions such as 1848 and wars of independence against established dynastic orders, so it rejected deference to existing institutions, though it revered tradition.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not a 19th-century issue; culture-based nationhood suggests some wariness, but Herder welcomed cultural exchange.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Mazzini imagined a brotherhood of free nations, but not supranational organs over them; his emphasis is on nations as units.

free-trade.rationale: Economics was unsettled; liberals favoured free trade while nationalist economists urged protection.

nation-first.rationale: Mazzini put duties to humanity before country and Herder ranked humankind above fatherland, though the later chauvinist strand disagreed.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Mazzini hoped free nations would aid oppressed peoples; this is inferred from his solidarity among peoples.

open-borders.rationale: Mazzini wanted borders to follow natural national divisions, so borders matter, even if he saw nations as harmonious.

limit-growth.rationale: An anachronistic question; romantic celebration of nature does not by itself yield a growth position.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the movement's doctrine.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The Romantic movement's reaction to Enlightenment rationalism suggests scepticism, though inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: The 1848 revolutions and independence wars like the Greek one were central romantic-nationalist actions against imperial rule.

experts-over-public.rationale: Mazzini wanted laws expressing the nation's whole will and a vote for every citizen, with the people's spirit, not experts, as the source of legitimacy.

central-planning.rationale: Mazzini rejected state-socialist command in favour of free association; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Mazzini's cooperatives fit this, but most adherents had no view; split.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Mazzini condemned privilege of birth, yet inheritance taxation was not his programme; split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalist economists such as List favoured tariffs but liberal romantic nationalists differed; split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No doctrine on the state's economic role; adherents split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mazzini's picture of a people of free, equal citizens with work suggests broad ownership; inferred, and romantic agrarian sentiment pointed the same way.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Mazzini explicitly opposed communism and class war, favouring labour associations within a national community.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions did not figure in the movement's programme, so neutral by silence.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Mazzini wanted harmony of labour and capital within the nation, but not state-recognised price-setting bodies; adherents split.

one-party-rule.rationale: Mazzini demanded popular franchise and laws from the whole nation's will, rejecting rule by a faction or caste.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Legitimacy was grounded in the nation and not in kings; Mazzini was a republican, though some strands accepted national monarchs.

democracy-best.rationale: Mazzini's nation requires a vote, education and work for all citizens, and Herder's mature politics was democratic; liberal strands dominate the core.

direct-votes.rationale: Mazzini wanted laws to express the people's will, but nothing indicates preference for referendums over representation.

workers-councils.rationale: Mazzini rejected class-based politics; the legitimate base of power is the nation of equals, not workers' bodies.

right-to-secede.rationale: Peoples had a right to leave multinational empires, such as Greeks, Hungarians and Poles, but the movement did not recognise it for every region within a nation-state.

natural-rulers.rationale: Mazzini denounced privilege of birth and accepted only the freely recognised privilege of genius joined with virtue.

political-violence-never.rationale: Armed uprisings, volunteer corps and wars of independence were a core means of the movement.

war-builds-character.rationale: Later strands glorified war, but Herder and Mazzini condemned militarised states; adherents split.

separate-church-state.rationale: National churches such as the Polish Catholic church were seen as bearers of the nation, but liberal strands favoured freedom of religion; leaning against strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Mazzini believed God underlies nations but wanted laws made by the people's will, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Nations organised in their own states under a national will; private provision of defence is foreign to the doctrine.

military-superiority.rationale: Herder opposed militarised states while later nationalists sought military power; split.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nationality is defined by shared language, culture, religion and customs of those born in it, but civic versions existed too and the strand sometimes added race.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Mazzini made nations and peoples, not classes, the agents of history and rejected class war.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Mazzini wanted equality of citizenship and rights, not of outcomes, since he accepted merit-based privilege of virtue.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from Herder's opposition to colonialism and his respect for each people's culture; the 19th-century movement did not address it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Herder opposed colonialism, but reparations are an anachronism with no doctrine behind them.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Slavism and pan-Germanism were offshoots; Mazzini wanted separate nations in brotherhood; split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mazzini warned against narrow egoism and called for duty and sacrifice to country and humanity.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Duties of Man argues that duties to humanity, country and family come before individual claims, and he preferred duty to a doctrine of rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Romanticism's reverence for nature and the landscape of the homeland suggests agreement, but it is inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy was never discussed by Herder, Mazzini or the Grimms, so neutral by silence.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Romantic revulsion against industrialisation existed, but nationalist movements typically wanted national industry; split.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The movement's rhetoric of organic tradition suggests disfavour, though it is inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from reverence for natural human character.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: legitimacy rests on the people's will and spirit, not on algorithms.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement revived the past to build a new national order, but liberal strands sought progress and freedom, not a return to lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Mazzini's creed of principle and duty is strongly ideological; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Conspiracy and uprising were means, but nationalists also fought elections and wrote constitutions in 1848; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Mazzini held that association and faith must prefigure the national community; weakly supported.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement sought modern nation-states with epics and literature, not a return to hunter-gatherer life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Mazzini's picture includes labour associations and work for all, not abolition of occupations.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Mazzini rejected communist distribution while wanting a minimum standard; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: The doctrine has no theory of production, and its adherents ranged from liberals to conservatives.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Mazzini rejected the Marxist reading of class and sought harmony of capital and labour.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Mazzini explicitly opposed class dictatorship, wanting laws from the whole nation's will.

collective-farming.rationale: Mazzini sought association by free choice and peasant landholding; coerced collectivisation is foreign; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Mazzini attributed war to dynastic conquests and distorted borders rather than to capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Duties to the national community are central, so a theft view of taxation is alien to it.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal nationalists accepted it, but the movement stressed duty and communal morals; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Peoples and nations hold collective rights to self-government, and Mazzini subordinated individual rights to duty.

conscription.rationale: Citizen armies defending the nation were widely admired, e.g. the levée en masse, Fichte's patriotism and Mazzini's call to sacrifice.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Mazzini made the vote and participation essential and demanded loyalty to one's country.

state-as-business.rationale: The nation is a community of equals, not a business serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Mazzini said a nation is not real while citizens lack education, work and the franchise.

media-academia-power.rationale: Anachronistic; intellectuals led the movement but no doctrine of this claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Herder rejected race as a category, though later strands racialised the nation; adherents split.

organic-representation.rationale: Romantic corporatist ideas existed on the conservative strand, but Mazzini wanted a direct national franchise; split.

total-state.rationale: Herder opposed a centralised, militarised state and Mazzini wanted free citizens; totalitarianism belongs to later fascism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Awakening, revival and resurrection of the nation, for instance Italy's Risorgimento, is the central romantic trope.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Mazzini and Herder condemned conquest as a distortion of natural borders and rejected imperialism, although some nationalists wanted Greater states.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The doctrine grounds legitimacy in the nation, not in lords or dynasties.

bound-labor.rationale: Mazzini condemned privilege of birth and demanded freedom; romantic nationalism stood against serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Herder's view that concepts vary by culture is relativist, but the claim about power is modern; split.

universal-morality.rationale: Herder denied morality is universal and grounded it in varying sentiment, but Mazzini believed in a universal law of God and humanity; adherents split.

single-common-good.rationale: Mazzini believed in a single national purpose and laws expressing the whole nation, opposing faction; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism descended from romantic nationalism, and general self-determination logic supports it; the strand itself rarely addressed it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from the idea that a nation belongs to its homeland; not directly addressed.

revive-national-language.rationale: The Brothers Grimm, Herder and the Finnish and Czech revivalists treated the national language as the vessel of the nation, and revived vernaculars as state languages.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Mazzini supported worker associations but this was not part of the movement's core; split.

school-vouchers.rationale: Unaddressed; Mazzini wanted national education, which leans against vouchers but is not decisive.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy was not part of the movement's concerns, so no position can be inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not a theme; liberal nationalists accepted it, others did not.

rule-by-example.rationale: Mazzini wanted the law as an expression of the nation's will, though he valued virtue; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-determination for each nationality against empire is the movement's core political claim.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; Mazzini favoured aiding peoples, but international law did not exist in its modern form.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The romantic reaction against Enlightenment rationalism exalted feeling, spirit and tradition; Herder criticised abstract rationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Anachronistic; culture-based nationhood suggests it, but 19th-century movements had no welfare states.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Mazzini made work a right and duty, but welfare conditions were not addressed.

class-collaboration.rationale: Mazzini urged capital and labour to cooperate in the national association and rejected class war.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural heritage, epics, folklore and monuments are the movement's raw material.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed by the 19th-century movement; later anti-colonial nationalists adopted it.

workers-nation.rationale: Mazzini opposed the international class framework and wanted workers to belong to their nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not a statement of the doctrine; adherents including Mazzini advocated women's education while folk tradition suggested roles; split.

ban-interest.rationale: The doctrine did not oppose interest; some conservative Romantics did, but not typical.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Herder rejected the concept of race and the typical movement did not seek racial segregation, though racialised strands existed.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The nation, not a class, is the basis of the state; Mazzini explicitly rejected class-based politics.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: An energy question from after the movement's era, with no principle that settles it.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationhood by shared language and culture implies cultural assimilation, although Herder valued cultural exchange.

elite-replacement.rationale: A modern conspiracy claim with no basis in the movement's doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Mazzini wanted a universal franchise but did not address electoral systems.

national-mission.rationale: Messianic strands such as Mickiewicz's Christ of Nations and Mazzini's Italy as leader of nations saw a mission for the nation, though Herder rejected favoured peoples.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Mazzini saw corrupt governments and ruling castes as obstacles to nations; populist tone.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics came after the classic movement; Herder's emphasis on humanity and rejection of race suggests rejection.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional-justice demands are modern and the movement never addressed them.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Mazzini wanted a state promoting education and work for all, so a minimal state is rejected; inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Herder rejected race categories and the cultural conception of nation does not need it; later racialised strands differed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Mazzini called for a community of free and equal people, yet romantic nationalism also ranked peoples, as in Fichte's German primacy; liberal core agrees.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialist doctrine, not applicable to nationalism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Herder opposed colonialism, but the question is not covered by the movement; split.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The unified nation-state with one law for all citizens fits the movement; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: National-church strands favoured it, liberal strands did not; split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A South Asian religious question; the movement had no position and no strand called for it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: National education often included religion in national culture; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mazzini wanted borders and law set by the free vote of the people rather than by kings, and legitimacy from the nation.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; mercantilism was not part of the doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: Herder opposed coercion, but later nationalism practised it; liberal core rejects it, with strands split.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Wars of liberation and uprisings contradict this principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Mazzini and Herder saw nations as cooperating parts of humanity, not competitors, though some strands favoured struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Liberal strands would oppose banning parties, while the conservative ones might back it, so neutral.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Mazzini's rejection of rule by caste and king is a republican idea of freedom, but he did not state it in these terms.

separated-powers.rationale: Not a theme of the movement; liberal constitutionalists agreed but others did not.

vanguard-party.rationale: Mazzini's conspiratorial societies were close to this, but he founded them on faith in the people and rejected class vanguards; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Mazzini called for education and work for the poor classes as pillars of the nation; moderate.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A modern British housing policy with no connection to the movement's concerns.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Mazzini preferred association and class harmony but did not discuss it.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Mazzini blamed political institutions and privilege; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cohesion rests on shared language and culture, which is why multinational empires were opposed, though Herder welcomed cultural exchange.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Mazzini favoured elected government and recognised virtue; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; liberal nationalists opposed, militarist ones favoured.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Market regulation of food prices was not part of its doctrine, so neutral.

party-controls-media.rationale: Liberal nationalists fought censorship under dynastic regimes.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army serves the nation under the people's will, not a party; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The movement defined nations by culture, but never set out naturalisation rules.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Nothing in Mazzini or Herder addresses the pay of representatives.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Mass party discipline was a later development outside the movement's own debates.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Mazzini wanted a federation of free nations with a Young Europe, but not sovereignty pooled in supranational bodies.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Republican nationalists like Mazzini opposed monarchical command; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: National churches differed in structure; split.

clerical-rule.rationale: Legitimacy came from the nation, not clergy, though Mazzini invoked God, and Mickiewicz's Catholic nation was not clerical government.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Workers should serve the nation, which is an international-class rejection.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Romantics prized artistic expression and folk poetry; censorship was a feature of the regimes they opposed.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Mazzini's republicanism and popular sovereignty make permanent office-holding uncongenial; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Popular recall was not a theme, although the people's will was central; neutral.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Mazzini favoured alliance among free peoples; unaddressed in the doctrine.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Unaddressed; inferred as rejection of a radical programme.

people-in-arms.rationale: Volunteer corps and armed citizenry, such as Garibaldi and Mazzini's national uprisings, were an ideal of the movement.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Folk culture and tradition of the peasantry, as collected by the Grimms, were treated as the authentic nation.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Unification of divided peoples, as in Germany and Italy, is a central goal.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Intellectuals led the movement while praising the unlettered folk; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Herder held that each culture has its own value and must be understood on its own terms, though Fichte-style strands claimed primacy.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from traditional cultural orientation.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The movement predates this dispute, and its religious adherents are not clearly for or against.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Nationality as those born within the culture favours descent over soil, as in German ethnic nationalism.

minority-language-support.rationale: Herder valued every people's language, but state-building nationalists often imposed one language; adherents genuinely split.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for minorities were not debated; nation-builders stressed shared law and culture.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Romantic cult of individual genius fits, but nationalism stresses communal custom; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt relief is a twentieth-century issue the movement did not meet.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The movement sought political independence first, not economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1848 Frankfurt Parliament and other national assemblies drafted constitutions for the nation, matching this demand.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberal nationalists prized freedoms; development dictatorship is a later idea.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Mazzini's duty to humanity suggests sympathy, but the movement did not address it.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement, and national independence is the only distant link.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Republican nationalists wanted popular sovereignty; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking policy was not part of the movement's thought.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Historic homeland claims were central to national narratives, such as Poland's partition grievances; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Mazzini subordinated private claims to social duty; inferred for property.

precautionary-principle.rationale: An environmental regulatory principle foreign to the era, so no inference is possible.

collective-defense.rationale: Mazzini imagined free nations as divisions of one army helping one another; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: National movements treated partitions and annexations without consent of the people as illegitimate, such as in Poland.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: National churches were an ally of national movements, e.g. in Poland; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The movement backed secession from empires but nation-states resisted it; split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy within a larger state was not a goal of a movement seeking national states; neutral.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The nation, not a sacred dynasty, is the source of legitimacy; Mazzini called birth privilege a usurpation.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design was not part of the movement's concerns, so neutral.

character-from-environment.rationale: Herder emphasised cultural formation of thought, but the Romantic stress on innate national spirit pulls the other way; split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Mazzini demanded law express the people's will and opposed rule of kings and castes.

space-expansion.rationale: Space travel was outside the era, and the movement's goals were national.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed; adherents were republicans or constitutional monarchists.

leader-cult.rationale: Mazzini's people of equals with God at summit conflicts with it, but later strands practised it; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is a modern question the movement never addressed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine that Mazzini's anti-class-war nationalism would reject.

land-redistribution.rationale: Peasant landholding appealed to some, but adherents split.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the attachment of a people to its homeland; not addressed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims to unify people of one language and culture across borders was a hallmark of German and Italian unification, though Herder rejected conquest.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The movement did not seek it, and liberal strands prized freedom of conscience.

women-must-cover.rationale: No basis in European romantic nationalism; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union was not discussed, though unification of German states did involve customs union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Slavic and pan-German ideas spun off from the language-and-ancestry idea of the nation; split on political union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Herder valued cultural autonomy, but the dominant aim was a state for each nation; adherents split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Romantic nationalism held that a people needs a homeland, for example through Zionism's origin and Polish exile; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Mazzini and Herder saw spirit, faith, culture and national character as the agents of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law was not in the movement's programme, so neutral.

no-bailouts.rationale: Government rescue of firms was not a concern of the movement.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Sovereignty of the people was central, but constitutional limits were not a debated point; split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement did not seek autarkic blocs; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Modern trade-agreement standards were unknown to the movement; no inference is possible.

moral-incentives.rationale: Mazzini's emphasis on duty and sacrifice over self-interest suggests it, but it was not an economic doctrine.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Mazzini's Young Italy and the expeditions that attempted to spark national risings relied on small armed groups.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Mazzini called privilege of birth a usurpation, though conservative strands retained monarchy and aristocracy; split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Mazzini and Herder tie national identity to a shared historical tradition and the movement revived national history and epics, so teaching it centrally fits, though Herder valued every culture.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Herder condemned colonial conquest and Mazzini blamed rulers for disfiguring Europe by conquest; each people has its own mission and the right to self-rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: Mazzini urges love of country and national education as a duty, and the movement made schooling in national language and tradition central.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race-conscious admissions were never addressed; inferred that adherents split between Mazzini-style equal citizenship and group-based redress.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary organisation was not addressed by the movement; adherents ranged from liberals to conservatives, so no stance is inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Mazzini rejected class struggle and socialist collapse theories in favour of national association; inferred from that anti-determinist stance.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The movement arose against imperial hegemony and Mazzini rejected conquest, so cultivating influence over ex-imperial lands is disfavoured; Polish messianists are an exception.

delink-world-market.rationale: Mazzini saw nations as cooperating parts of humanity; economic delinking was not a theme, and the inference is a mild no.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Mazzini held that all classes of a nation share duties and interests and rejected class division; this Leninist idea is inferred to be foreign to it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Mazzini demanded equal rights and rejected birth privilege, so inferred disapproval of private discrimination; the issue itself was never addressed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Mazzini stressed duties over rights, but 1848 liberal nationalists pressed for written constitutions; inferred mild support.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Mazzini's nations are God-given units, so treaties that split a people against its will lack legitimacy.

elective-rulers.rationale: Mazzini's republican strand rejects birth privilege and bases authority on the will of the people.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: the strand grounds legitimacy in the organic unity and will of the people, so it does not let a dissenter block it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Mazzini and the liberal strand ground rule in the will of the people, which a ruler who betrays it forfeits.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream liberal-democratic strand of 1848 favoured representative assemblies over crowns.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Herder's respect for living peoples and his rejection of universal reason suggest sympathy with sentient beings; not addressed directly.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: nineteenth-century nationalists did not question humane use of animals; not addressed.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Mazzini's Duties of Man stresses duty to fellow countrymen and to the poorer classes.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Mazzini calls on citizens to take part in the national cause as a duty, which rules out withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: nationalists regard national culture as a source of liberation, not a means of pacifying the people.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: the strand takes culture as a carrier of the national spirit, not as a ruling-class device.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: Herder opposed colonialism but the strand has no theory of surplus transfer; the question is anachronistic.

native-born-offices.rationale: Genuinely split: the liberal strand around Mazzini admits all citizens, while the cultural and racialised strand reserves national life for the native nation.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from national self-determination: each nation, including a socialist movement, should find its own path.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national self-determination and national character, though Mazzini also favoured fraternal cooperation among nations.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Wikipedia notes that romantic nationalism fed demands for unifying all members of a nation, including irredentism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Herder was an anti-colonial critic of conquest, and Mazzini asked for equality among citizens; the statement is not addressed directly.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic: the question belongs to the twentieth century, and the liberal strand held no such constitutional concept.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic and split: the liberal strand would condemn tyranny of any kind, but the strand's later chauvinist wing would not.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: the strand predates the war's interpretation debates, and its liberal-republican mainstream was anti-slavery.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The cult of national history, heroes and epics is central to the movement, which suggests preserving its memorials.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Anachronistic: gender-specific programmes were no concern of the movement.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Anachronistic: the question was not posed, and the sources give no basis for either side.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Herder's cultural pluralism holds that each people develops its own forms and values, and that no one culture's institutions are universal.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the liberal strand's republicanism, which favoured citizen militias and civil rule over a political army.

paid-care-work.rationale: Anachronistic: Mazzini placed woman's duties in education and the home, and the strand did not call for paid care work.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from Mazzini's picture of family as the first school of duty and the romantic reverence for tradition and the organic community.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream strand's democratic, popular-sovereignty ideal, which makes office a matter of the people's choice rather than examined expertise.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic policy was largely unaddressed; the strand mixed liberal openness with protection of the national economy (List).

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; romantic nationalists held conservative family views in many cases but liberal democrats such as Mazzini did not make it an issue.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not addressed; the strand favoured representative republics and popular sovereignty but has no documented stance on recall.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Anachronistic; Mazzini wanted association and workers' cooperation but no pension system was in view.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the liberal strand's acceptance of property rights; Mazzini backed associations of workers, not communal tenure conditional on use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the 1848 liberal-democratic demand for constitutions and elected national assemblies with control over the state.

single-official-language.rationale: Language as the carrier of the national spirit was central for Herder and the Grimms, and national movements pressed for the vernacular in schooling and public life, though some tolerated minorities.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the nation's claim to its territory was central but restriction of foreign property was not a defined plank.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the strand's focus on national rather than racial-group equality and its liberal concern with intent and equal rights.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from Mazzini's call to place duty and ideals above material well-being and from romantic distrust of commercial materialism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the strand's support for other peoples' national risings, as in Mazzini's Young Europe, though state arming was rarely discussed.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Self-determination of every nation was core, so a great power forcing an ally to stay would violate national freedom.

corporate-influence.rationale: Economic power was not a concern of the movement, which centred on language and culture; nothing here supports a firm position.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Nineteenth-century nationalists feared foreign domination but also valued a free press and association; adherents had no common doctrine on foreign money.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy was not addressed; inferred only from the movement's concern for the people's continuity, which is too general to settle a side.

residents-only-property.rationale: The movement tied peoples to their homeland but never addressed local property limits; liberal and conservative adherents would differ.

job-guarantee.rationale: Mazzini held that work and education should be secured to every citizen; a state job guarantee is inferred from that, not stated.

democratic-peace.rationale: Mazzini expected free, republican nations to live in brotherhood and peace; the democratic-peace claim itself is an inference.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Mazzini stressed duties and obedience to the nation's just law while allowing revolt against tyranny, so adherents would mostly reject a general freedom from obeying law.

non-intervention.rationale: Herder rejected colonial domination of peoples, but Mazzini backed mutual aid among nations and 1848 nationalists sought foreign help; an absolute ban is inferred as unlikely.

industrial-unions.rationale: Mazzini favoured worker association but the movement had no doctrine on union structure; inferred as indifferent.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The mainstream liberal strand held that every nation deserves equal respect and rejected birth privilege; minority-plot claims belong to the chauvinist strand excluded from scope.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Mazzini treated the family as the basis of society and moral duty; abolishing legal marriage is inferred as foreign to the movement.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Mazzini's republican insistence on the will of the people and a free educated citizenry implies open access to government, though not stated.

local-production.rationale: The movement valued native land and customs but never addressed local-versus-distant production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Mazzini's own nationalism was run through formal organisations such as Young Italy and mass national movements, so small informal cells are not its model.

national-law-over-international.rationale: National self-determination and the will of the people imply the nation's own law is the last word; international courts post-date the movement, so this is inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: The mainstream strand defined nation by language, culture and history rather than faith; only variants such as Mickiewicz's Polish messianism made religion central.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Mazzini and Herder treat nations as equals in a fraternity of peoples, so ritual submission to a leading power is inferred to be unwelcome.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A unitary national republic with equal citizens is inferred from Mazzini; regional revenue retention is not addressed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Mazzini opposed communism and defended property earned by labour, so common ownership of the means of production is inferred to be rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Nineteenth-century nationalists did not address communist states as a bloc; Mazzini opposed communism as a doctrine but stressed peaceful fraternity of peoples.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery models are not addressed; nothing in Mazzini or Herder favours or rules out a public-private mix.

religion-illusion.rationale: Mazzini grounds nations and duties in God and Providence, and religion is central to the movement, so religion as a mere illusion is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Mainstream liberal nationalists backed the bourgeois, free-market order of the 1848 era; this is inferred from the liberal strand, not stated.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Mazzini asked for equal rights and education for women within the republic, not a transformed economic system; this is inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Family-centred domestic life is assumed in Mazzini's writing; public provision of housework is not addressed and is inferred to be unwelcome.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language is the carrier of the national spirit for Herder and Fichte, and purist language reform was common in the movement, though the liberal strand was split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Respect for peoples' rights and Herder's cultural pluralism suggest lasting commitments to distinct nations; treaties are not directly addressed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Mazzini favoured the nation as the framework of self-government rather than small communes holding property in common; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Herder's cultural pluralism and anti-colonialism imply peoples should keep their own homelands; state-steered settlement is inferred to be rejected by the liberal strand.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Mazzini rejected both communism and unregulated individualism in favour of association and duty, an inferred third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Romantic nationalists grounded claims in shared history and homeland, but Mazzini and Herder stressed the free will of peoples; inferred, not stated as a land-claim rule.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the mainstream liberal strand in scope would reject it, and the racial strand is excluded.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic: the sources never address it, and 19th-century adherents would have been split.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mazzini bases legitimacy on the will of the people, equal rights and the franchise, which excludes suppressing opposition for order.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed; Mazzini's religion is of conscience and duty rather than state enforcement, but Mickiewicz's messianism could split adherents.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Herder is described as anti-colonial and held that peoples should not be ruled for another's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Outside the movement's scope; no basis for a position.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Mazzini's popular-sovereignty politics, which rules out religious tests of legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not stated as a method; inferred from Mazzini's emphasis on popular will, education and the franchise.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; the movement centred on nation, not race-sex-class intersections.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources never address it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; the movement united liberal and conservative strands around the nation.

alienated-labor.rationale: Not addressed; no stated view on labour and creative activity.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Herder's cultural pluralism values each people's culture equally, so incompatibility claims fit poorly; the racial strand is excluded.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Mazzini calls nations God-given units yet bases government on the will of the people, so the movement is split on the source of authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; the question is anachronistic for the period.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources do not discuss it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Mazzini wanted education and work guaranteed to citizens, which suggests a social floor; the market question is inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Mazzini's duties include national service, and nations needed defending to be free; inferred rather than stated.

rich-first.rationale: Mazzini rejects birth privilege and stresses equality of citizens; inferred, not stated on wealth.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; Mazzini's humanity-before-country ethic and national freedom needs could point either way.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Mazzini rejected privilege of birth and wanted republican government by the will of the people.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mazzini favoured workers' associations and cooperation; at-cost mutual credit is inferred from that.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: National independence and self-rule are central, so refusing foreign lender dictation is inferred; the issue is anachronistic.

property-franchise.rationale: Mazzini demanded equal citizenship and universal franchise, rejecting privilege tied to wealth.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Mazzini backed women's equality while Herder's nature-culture views are not framed this way; not addressed.

reification.rationale: A Marxian idea; romantic nationalists distrusted materialism but did not analyse commodity relations; inferred split.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Mazzini valued a free press but also stressed education and association; the wealth critique is not addressed.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Herder's and Mazzini's liberal-republican strand favoured government under law and the will of the people over arbitrary rule.

racial-franchise.rationale: Mainstream romantic nationalism defined the nation by language and culture, not race, and Herder explicitly rejected racial hierarchy.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement never addressed the internet and adherents' views cannot be inferred either way.

open-government-data.rationale: Mazzini's open, popular government implies public accountability; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Mazzini's religion of duty to humanity was inclusive in spirit, though some variants (Mickiewicz) were confessional; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Mainstream liberal romantic nationalism placed duty to humanity above narrow patriotism, so shunning a minority is inferred as contrary.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Mazzini sought an elected national assembly and universal suffrage; lot-selected bodies are not addressed, so this is inferred from his representative republicanism.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Herder and Mazzini treated faith as a source of national and moral renewal, while Mickiewicz-style messianism leaned on tradition; adherents were split and no source addresses reinterpretation directly.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Mazzini opposed the domination of labour by capital and wanted association among workers, so concentrated wealth is inferred as a threat to citizens' equal liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: A nineteenth-century movement that never addressed this; modern heirs are split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Mazzini and Herder tie nations to a spiritual mission under God, so a state programme of atheism is contrary to the strand.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nineteenth-century nationalists assumed a state with law and order; abolition is anachronistic and inferred as strongly opposed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The strand holds that each nation should form its own unified state, so it favours national majority self-government over consociational sharing; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Mazzini favoured both association and moral duty to the poor and state education and work; adherents are split and the sources do not say.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by this movement; adherents had no common view.

vote-delegation.rationale: Mazzini's republicanism stressed national unity and duty, so he is unlikely to favour fragmented delegated voting; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: An anachronistic question for a nineteenth-century movement, with no inferable stance.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Nineteenth-century romantic nationalists lived in an era of male-only clergy and did not question it; inferred and anachronistic.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Mazzini advocated women's moral equality in some writings but the era assumed male household authority; adherents inferred as mildly traditional.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; the liberal-cultural strand defends citizens' rights while defining the nation by a shared people, so adherents split on extending the vote to foreigners.

rent-control.rationale: Housing markets were not an issue for the movement; inferred nothing definite from its principles.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: Romantic nationalists prized authors and national epics, and copyright for writers arose in their era, but abolition was never proposed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: youth gymnastic and student societies (Turnvereine, Young Italy) existed, but drilled uniformed national-service movements belong to later strands.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; nuclear weapons postdate the movement and its principles give no direction.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the demand for national self-determination and freedom from foreign rule; foreign troops on national soil would offend a people's sovereignty.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: Mazzini's duty to humanity and solidarity with oppressed peoples (e.g. Poland) favours recognising wrongs done to a nation, though genocide recognition is a later practice.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Mazzini's Duties of Man treats labour as the source of wealth and the basis of association; the mainstream strand was liberal-democratic and sympathetic to workers over idle privilege.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: Mazzini and 1848 nationalists justified armed struggle for the nation and defence of the oppressed, so absolute pacifism was not their view.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Herder and the movement stressed a people's identity rooted in ancient language, folklore and history; scholars also note this continuity was partly constructed, so not strongly.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; the movement concerned nations, not sex and gender theory.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic to feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Romantic nationalism honoured national martyrs, such as Polish and Italian patriots, and Mickiewicz's messianism cast Poland's sufferers as martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Mickiewicz's and Mazzini's strands framed politics as a religious mission, but the liberal mainstream did not cast it as good against evil; adherents differ.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: the nation as a cultural community suits a homeland serving as a cultural centre, but unification was the stated aim for a people's territory.

culture-before-state.rationale: Herder and the folklore project made cultural and linguistic revival the foundation of national awakening, preceding political statehood.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; Mazzini spoke of God and Humanity, but the movement said nothing on gendered descriptions of God.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The mainstream liberal strand sought equal citizenship; the exclusionary economic nationalism of the racialised strand is outside the scope and so only a mild no.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The movement demanded that the territory of a people be united in one state; 'single unit' is read as that unification, a core demand of Mazzini and the 1848 revolutions.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Mazzini's support for workers' associations and liberal freedoms.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Mazzini rejected class struggle and socialism in favour of national unity; inferred for the mainstream strand.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the duty-based, solidaristic view of the nation in The Duties of Man.

second-chamber.rationale: Mainstream liberal nationalists of 1848 favoured constitutional parliaments, often with two chambers; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Mazzini favoured association and cooperation but with the nation as the frame; inferred as not municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Mazzini argued for a unitary nation against federalism and local particularism; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Mazzini's concern for fair pay and the dignity of labour.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's progressive, humanitarian faith in improvement.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; Herder's belief in human perfectibility suggests openness, but the topic was not addressed.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; the liberal strand valued civil liberty, so freedom from state tracing is inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the liberal strand's defence of free expression against censorship.

person-over-state.rationale: Mazzini's Duties of Man ties the individual to duties towards country and humanity; inferred that the person is not the sole end.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Mazzini grounds the nation in duty to God and humanity, and Mickiewicz's messianism is explicitly religious.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: A unitary nation-state is favoured over regional autonomy, so powers would be national grants; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Romantic reverence for nature and rural folk life.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Romantic valuing of rural folk culture as the carrier of the national spirit.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The mainstream liberal strand defines the nation by language and culture, not race, with racial thinking a later offshoot.

racial-pride.rationale: The strand prizes national pride but defines it by culture and not race; inferred as agreement for ancestry and heritage.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Mazzini backed wars of national liberation, which are not purely defensive; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Herder held that language carries a people's spirit and makes the nation, and the movement demanded unity for peoples split by borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: Mazzini's republican nationalism rests on one citizenry under equal rights; separate religious electorates are inferred to conflict with that.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from the movement's grievance over partitioned nations such as Poland, Italy and Germany under dynastic rule.

free-public-college.rationale: Mazzini wanted education guaranteed to every citizen; free college is an extension and not stated.

pollution-taxes.rationale: A nineteenth-century movement that never addressed pollution taxes, with nothing in its principles pointing either way.

future-generations.rationale: Mazzini framed duties to humanity, family and country as handed on across generations; inferred from that.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed; Mazzini backed women's equal rights, which cuts against a distinct-values claim, while Herder's organic view of roles points the other way.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from Mazzini's vision of a brotherhood of free nations, which leaves little room for armed rivalry.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the liberal, republican strand's hostility to the dynastic cabinet diplomacy of the Holy Alliance.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from liberal-republican economics of the era, which favoured free commerce; the sources do not discuss capital flows.

missingStatements.text: The folk songs, tales and epics of a people are the truest expression of its identity and should be collected and valued.
missingStatements.rationale: The Grimms' tales, Herder's folk song collection and national epics like the Kalevala are the movement's signature project.

missingStatements.text: Each nation has a distinctive character or spirit that its language carries and that politics should respect.
missingStatements.rationale: Herder and Fichte tied national spirit to language, and the movement's legitimacy claims rest on it.

missingStatements.text: Borders should follow the natural divisions of peoples rather than the claims of dynasties.
missingStatements.rationale: Mazzini says borders should follow national divisions and the free vote of peoples, not kings or conquest.

notes: Adherents split between the liberal-cosmopolitan strand (Herder, Mazzini), which rejects race, empire and war, and the racialised, chauvinist strand (late Fichte, volkisch movements). Answers follow the former where they differ, with zero used where the split is real.
